name: San Antonio de Espasante
notes: Sheltered beach at the mouth of the Ortigueira estuary with a local surf school.

name: Picón
notes: Cliff-backed beach below Loiba, exposed to north swells.

name: Vilarrube
notes: Estuary-mouth beach that only gets smaller surf; useful when Pantín is too big.

name: Pantín
notes: Host of the Pantín Classic; rights and lefts by the rocks at the north end.

name: Frouxeira
notes: Long open beach with shifting sandbars.

name: Campelo
notes: Small cliff-backed cove with fast peaks that works on small swells.

name: Ponzos
notes: Rural beach with long waves; currents when the sea is big.

name: Santa Comba
notes: Straight beach below the Santa Comba islet chapel, best at low tide.

name: Esmelle
notes: Smaller beach that holds well when the sea is moderate.

name: San Xurxo
notes: Wide bay used by surf schools; a left at one end.

name: Doniños
notes: Two-kilometre beach near Ferrol with several sandbar peaks, Outeiro at the north end.

name: Penencia
notes: Quieter south end of Doniños below the Penencia point.

name: Chanteiro
notes: Inner-estuary beach that only breaks on big north-west swells.

name: Ondalonga (Pedrido)
notes: Very long, slow wave at the mouth of the Betanzos estuary that needs a big swell; longboard spot.

name: Bastiagueiro
notes: Sheltered bay beach in Oleiros that works on large north-west swells.

name: Orzán
notes: A Coruña's city beach, a winter classic with several sandbar peaks.

name: O Matadoiro
notes: Right-hander off the rocks at the east end of Orzán.

name: Sabón
notes: Arteixo beach with long waves over wide sandbanks; surf schools.

name: Barrañán
notes: Popular Arteixo beach with variable peaks over sand and rock.

name: Caión
notes: Two main peaks, a central one and a right sheltered by the harbour wall.

name: Baldaio
notes: Long dune beach in the Razo-Baldaio natural area.

name: Razo
notes: Long beach break with peaks along its whole length; surf-camp hub of the region.

name: Malpica (Area Maior)
notes: Town beach with a left by the rocks and a right towards the centre.

name: Soesto
notes: One of the most consistent beaches on the Costa da Morte, picks up small swells.

name: Traba
notes: Long dune beach next to a lagoon between Laxe and Camariñas.

name: Moreira
notes: Cove under Cape Touriñán.

name: Nemiña
notes: Wild beach sheltered from north winds, rights and lefts over sand.

name: Lires
notes: Left at the river mouth at the south end of the Nemiña bay.

name: O Rostro
notes: Fully exposed two-kilometre beach with several fast peaks.

name: Mar de Fóra
notes: Exposed beach on the open side of Cape Fisterra; dangerous currents.

name: Estorde
notes: Sheltered beach in the Corcubión estuary that only breaks on big swells.

name: Carnota
notes: Seven-kilometre dune beach, one of the longest in Galicia.

name: Lariño
notes: Short, powerful waves over sand and rock.

name: Louro
notes: Beach below Monte Louro at the mouth of the Muros estuary.

name: Aguieira
notes: Long beach inside the Muros-Noia estuary mouth; small surf, used for kite and windsurf.

name: Río Sieira
notes: Consistent beach backed by the Coviña pine wood, popular with Santiago surfers.

name: As Furnas
notes: Wild beach with strong waves that breaks on little swell.

name: A Ladeira (Corrubedo)
notes: Corrubedo beach sheltered from north winds; surf school on site.

name: A Lanzada
notes: Two-and-a-half-kilometre open beach on the O Grove isthmus; easy waves on the rising tide.

name: Montalvo
notes: Needs a groundswell; left at Punta Montalvo and a right at the other end.

name: Nerga
notes: Beach at the mouth of the Vigo estuary that needs a big swell.

name: O Vao
notes: Vigo city beach that only works on big winter swells.

name: Patos
notes: Nigrán beach facing the Cíes Islands, the surf hub of the Vigo area.

name: Pico de Patos
notes: Fast right and left over rock at the west end of Patos.

name: Praia América
notes: Long beach in the Baiona bay that needs a large swell to break.

name: A Esquerda de Oia
notes: Powerful left over rock in front of the Santa María de Oia monastery.

name: Punta del Moral
notes: Peaks next to the Guadiana breakwater; works in winter with south-west swell.

name: Isla Cristina
notes: Variable peaks up to about a metre in autumn and winter.

name: El Portil
notes: Calm water behind the El Rompido sand spit, used for kite lessons.

name: Punta Umbría
notes: Urban beach break; winter swell with westerly winds.

name: Mazagón
notes: Best-known surf beach in Huelva, with occasional hollow rights and lefts in winter.

name: Matalascañas (Torre de la Higuera)
notes: Gentle sandbar waves at the north end of Matalascañas beside the toppled tower.

name: Punta Candor
notes: Rota's most exposed stretch, used for surf and bodyboard.

name: Valdelagrana
notes: Bay beach with a regular afternoon westerly; flat-water kite and windsurf.

name: Santa María del Mar
notes: Small city beach below the old town; crowded with locals.

name: La Cabañita (La Victoria)
notes: Peak over rock slabs on La Victoria beach, best in autumn and winter.

name: Cortadura
notes: Urban beach break along the isthmus, works on all tides.

name: Camposoto
notes: Nine-kilometre natural beach in San Fernando, known for windsurf.

name: Sancti Petri
notes: Thermal westerly of up to about 20 knots on summer afternoons.

name: Roche
notes: Cliff coves sheltered from the Levante; hollow at low tide, shorebreak at high tide.

name: Fuente del Gallo
notes: Cove north of Conil with a mellow right, good for longboards.

name: La Fontanilla
notes: Several peaks in front of the car park and a right off the rocks.

name: Castilnovo
notes: Wild beach south of Conil known for windsurf.

name: El Palmar
notes: Eight kilometres of sandbar peaks; the surf centre of Cádiz with many schools.

name: Zahora
notes: Several peaks over a rocky bottom, mainly a winter spot.

name: Los Caños de Meca
notes: Reef and point waves beside Cape Trafalgar; a strong-Levante kite alternative.

name: Hierbabuena
notes: Long right over reef below the Barbate cliffs; walk-in access.

name: Bolonia
notes: Dune-backed bay; kite zone in front of the La Cabaña beach bar.

name: Punta Paloma
notes: Right-hand point wave in winter storms; kite at the dune end of Valdevaqueros.

name: Valdevaqueros
notes: Main Levante kite beach, sheltered by Punta Paloma; rocks at the south end.

name: Los Lances Norte
notes: Main kite zone between Río Jara and the Valdevaqueros end; rescue boats in Levante.

name: Río Jara
notes: River-mouth area of Los Lances; gusty Levante, kiting off-season only.

name: Los Lances Sur
notes: Town end of Los Lances; Poniente kite spot and winter beach break.

name: Balneario
notes: Beside the Tarifa causeway; offshore Levante for experienced riders only.
